mechanism_narrative: A decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) indicates an active monetary easing policy, which reduces the discount rate for equity valuation, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of periods where FEDFUNDS declines by at least 0.1 percentage points over the prior month, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 in a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) exceeds 9.0% for two consecutive months, it signals a severe labor market downturn that triggers a flight to quality and risk-off sentiment, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where UNRATE exceeds 9.0% for two consecutive months, or the Rank IC is negative over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicates a broad-based weakening in consumer demand, which leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to reduced corporate revenue expectations.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of periods where both HOUST and RSAFS decline by at least 1.0% from the prior month, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 in a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) declines by more than 0.5% from the prior month, it signals a contraction in the manufacturing sector, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings face headwinds.
failure_condition: The 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where INDPRO declines by more than 0.5% from the prior month, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 in a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A rising consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) indicates persistent inflation, which typically leads to a reduction in real equity valuations and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of periods where CPIAUCSL rises by at least 0.2% from the prior month, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 in a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) exceeds 4.5%, it signals a restrictive monetary policy that increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS exceeds 4.5%, or the Rank IC is negative over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in employment (PAYEMS) and decrease in unemployment (UNRATE) indicates a strong labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate hiring supports revenue growth.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of periods where PAYEMS increases by at least 0.5% and UNRATE decreases by at least 0.1% from the prior month, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 in a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of strong consumer spending (RSAFS above 380,000 million dollars), the S&P 500 experiences positive returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings are supported by robust retail activity.
failure_condition: The 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of instances where RSAFS exceeds 380,000 million dollars, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 in a 3-year rolling window.
